chunks: Abi (rah) narrated from Sa'd ibn Abdillah from Salamah ibn al-Khattab from Isma'il ibn Ishaq from Isma'il ibn Aban from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim from al-Sadiq from his father from his ancestors (peace be upon them) who said:

Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) said: 'And there is no believer, man or woman, who places his hand on the head of an orphan with mercy for him, except that Allah writes for him a good deed for every hair that his hand passed over.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for stroking an orphan's head with mercy?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Thawab al-A'mal*, this hadith establishes a tangible spiritual metric for compassion, linking the physical act of stroking an orphan's head to the accumulation of individual good deeds. It underscores the Shia emphasis on *tarahhum* (mercy) as the motivating intent, transforming a simple gesture into a sustained source of divine reward.
